description.narrative: Soil Values aims to enable small-scale food producers in the Sahel (women, men, and youth) to sustainably manage soil fertility to improve ecologically sustainable food production and increase resilience to climate change and shocks. More concretely, in terms of impact, after 10 years of implementation, Soil Values will ensure that sustainable soil fertility management is a mainstay of farming systems in the Sahel, improving the soil fertility and production capacity of 2 million hectares of farmland in the Sahel, as well as the resilience and well-being of 1.5 million small-scale food producers, particularly women, in Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and northern Nigeria

Soil Values is a 10-tear program that will work through three pathways to change, each representing a different area of action (1) the agroecological pathway, (2) the inclusive market development pathway (markets and finance), and (3) the enabling environment pathway (institutions and policies). The agroecological pathway targets small-scale food producers and farming systems, as well as the landscapes and watersheds that surround them. The inclusive market development path focuses on the private sector (markets, investments, business models) to overcome market barriers and strengthen relevant markets, and on financing institutions to invest in soil fertility. Finally, the enabling environment pathway focuses on the ability of public sector institutions, policies, and governance structures to support soil health in the long term.
Soil Values targets small-scale food producers, particularly women and youth, in Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Nigeria (northern)

Soil Values will work through the following five areas of intervention:1-Bundling: grouping of technical and socio-economic interventions into combined packages to address soil fertility management at farm level in the broadest possible sense. 2-Integrate our interventions at landscape and watershed level to optimize water management and nutrient use efficiency, introduce nature-based solutions for landscape greening, and create participatory, co-designed plans at community level for sustainable natural resource management. 3-Brokering for long-term investment in soil fertility management, and identifying payment mechanisms for small-scale food producers, including livestock farmers and breeders. 4-Convening to stimulate a favorable policy environment at regional, national, and sub-national levels. 5-Scoping and learning to integrate lessons learned from the program and other initiatives, and build capacity of key stakeholders.

description.narrative: The Soil Health Index is an indicator designed to assess the condition of soil by gathering both observational data and the subjective perceptions of farmers. It evaluates three key areas: chemical properties (such as nutrient balance and pH), physical properties (such as soil texture and erosion), and biological properties (like the presence of organic matter and soil life). Farmers rate their agreement with specific statements about these aspects on a scale from "strongly agree" to "strongly disagree." Each response is scored and weighted to reflect its relative importance in determining overall soil health. The final score, calculated as a weighted average, provides a comprehensive assessment of soil health, with higher scores indicating more favorable conditions.
